info.title: sLaunch
info.author: etonedemid
info.details: sLaunch is a fast text based HOME menu replacement inspired by niagara launcher.

changelog:
v1.4.0
Plug the console into a computer and copy files straight onto the SD card,
manage them on the console with a new file manager, and watch clips and play
music in real players. Box art now comes from GameTDB, full printed box scans
included, and loads without stutter.

 USB file transfer

While the menu is on screen, plugging the console into a computer shows the SD
card as an MTP device ("Nintendo Switch"). Windows and most Linux file managers
support MTP out of the box; macOS needs an MTP client such as OpenMTP.

- A USB- tag sits in the top bar while a computer is connected.
- A card at the top right shows what is moving: the file, receiving or sending,
  percentage, size and speed, then a summary once it is done.
- Auto-sleep is held off while a computer is connected.
- The server stops whenever the menu hands off to a game, homebrew or a system
  applet, so homebrew that uses USB itself (DBI, Goldleaf, ...) gets it free. A
  copy still running at that moment is cut off.

The server is Atmosphère's own haze, running inside the menu.

 File manager

Browse the SD card from the menu: copy, move, rename, delete and make folders.

 Album and music

- The album plays video clips, with sound, pause and seeking, and has a proper
  photo viewer with a slideshow.
- Music has a full player: album art, the track list, seeking, repeat, shuffle
  and volume.

 Box art

- Box art comes from GameTDB: https://www.gametdb.com/ first, with no key
  needed, including full printed box scans (back, spine and front) that Flow
  wraps around its cases. Pick the region under Theming.
- SteamGridDB is optional now, and only asked when you turn it on and set a key.
- A progress bar shows what is being fetched.
- Art is read and decoded on a background thread, so landing on a game no longer
  stutters, and it loads noticeably faster.

 Layouts and looks

- Flow is real 3D: solid boxes with lighting and reflections.
- Grid is styled after Windows 10 Mobile tiles; Shelf after the Xbox 360.
- New Ocean background, hills for Retrowave, and every background and effect
  now runs on the GPU.
- First-run setup is simpler, with a gallery of screenshots to pick a layout.
- The theme editor saves when you close it, and Themes marks the theme you are
  actually using as current.

 Fixes

- Red and blue were swapped in game icons and overlays.
- Crashes from images that failed to decode, and from long browsing through big
  ROM libraries.
- Some games showed another game's Steam news and screenshots.
- Choppy audio in album clips.

 Install

Copy the contents of slaunch-v1.4.0-sd.zip to the root of your SD card, or
run sInstaller.nro from the homebrew menu.

v1.3.0
Two people can now share a console without sharing a menu, and homebrew can
hand over to other homebrew.

 Settings are per user

Everything you choose belongs to the Switch account that chose it - theme and
your own custom themes, font, icon pack, UI mode, layout tuning, tile sizes and
colours, favourites, manual order, renamed entries, hidden system entries,
pinned homebrew, widget placement and music. They live in


slaunch/config/users//


with a name.txt inside holding the nickname, so you can tell the folders
apart from a PC. Content stays shared, because it is content: themes/,
icon_packs/, fonts/, music/, widgets/, covers/, lang/. So does
anything that belongs to the console rather than a person - the SteamGridDB
key, the homebrew donor title, takeover.txt.

Updating loses nothing. The first account to open the menu inherits your
existing slaunch/config/ files, first-run setup included, so it sees exactly
what it saw before. The originals are copied rather than moved, so downgrading
still finds them, and a marker stops a second account from inheriting them too
- new accounts start on the defaults and go through setup once.

 Homebrew that launches homebrew

An .nro handing over to another one works as it always has. What it could not
do is change the terms it runs under: homebrew started from the Homebrew menu
lives in an applet slot with a small heap, and no process can promote itself to
a full-RAM application. So the daemon now watches a drop box:


sdmc:/slaunch/hb_queue/.req      mode=app | nro=... | argv=... | donor=...


Any homebrew can write one with plain stdio - the format and a ready-made
writer are in libs/sCommon/include/sl/sys/HbLaunchRequest.hpp. The daemon
takes it the moment the homebrew that queued it exits, never while it is still
on screen, and chains straight into the next launch instead of bouncing through
the menu. Leave donor= out and it uses the donor set in Homebrew > Set donor.
Requests are one-shot and deleted as they are taken, so a bad one costs a
launch rather than a boot loop.

To get this for homebrew that knows nothing about sLaunch, create
sdmc:/slaunch/config/hb_chain_app.txt containing 1, and every chainload out
of an applet slot is handed to the daemon, so what hbmenu opens runs with full
RAM. It is opt-in because it changes where those launches happen: you come back
to sLaunch rather than to the homebrew you came from.

Arguments now survive a launch as well - they used to be collected and dropped.

 Also

- NetSurf is filed under Network- in XMB, next to the browser, instead of
  sitting with the rest of the homebrew.
- An optional content filter for the covers and news the menu fetches, off
  unless slaunch/config/content_filter.txt says enabled=1. See
  docs/CONTENT_FILTER.md: docs/CONTENT_FILTER.md.
- The crypto, countdown and quote widgets are back in the build - a clean
  build had been quietly shipping without them.

 Install

Copy the contents of slaunch-v1.3.0-sd.zip to the root of your SD card, or
run sInstaller.nro from the homebrew menu.

v1.1.0
Firmware compat
rendering fixes

v1.0.0
Grid rebuilt as a tile wall: three tile sizes, per-entry colour, home widgets embeddable as live tiles, adjustable columns and rows.

Widgets receive the height of the box they are drawn in and lay out to it.

Adds a desktop simulator (projects/sMenu/sim) that builds the shipping sources against a stubbed libnx for Linux and Windows.

Locale files brought to full coverage.

 Install

Copy the contents of slaunch-v1.0.0-sd.zip to the root of your SD card, or run sInstaller.nro from the homebrew menu.

v0.9.0
sLaunch v0.9.0

The coverflow release. There is a new UI mode that draws your games as 3D boxes
you can turn around, XMB has been rebuilt to match the real thing and is now the
default, and the menu no longer freezes for a few seconds every time you press
HOME.

 Flow - a new UI mode

A shelf of 3D game boxes, in the spirit of WiiFlow and Aurora.

- Real boxes with a front, a back and two edges, not rotated flat covers. Turn
  one around with the right stick and you can read the back of the case.
- Box art is fetched automatically from SteamGridDB. Put your API key in
  Theming > SteamGridDB key and covers appear as you browse. Art is saved to
  slaunch/covers/ and only fetched once per game.
- Two images across the top of the back of each case.
- Reflections, and a Nintendo Switch box wrap printed over every box.
- Games and homebrew live on the shelf; everything else (Settings, Media, Power)
  is one press of Minus away.
- Flow layout is yours to tune.- Theming > Flow layout gives you box size and
  thickness, spacing, turn angle, camera distance and depth falloff, adjusted
  live against the shelf itself and saved to slaunch/config/flow.txt.

If you have no cover for a game yet, its box shows the game's own icon rather
than sitting blank.

 XMB, rebuilt

XMB is now the default layout, and it is a much closer match to the real thing:
the left-anchored geometry, the uneven row spacing, the fade as rows pass behind
the category bar, and the same proportions throughout.

- Every submenu now wears the XMB look too, instead of dropping you into a
  different-looking list.
- The Homebrew category lists every .nro on your card, not only the ones you
  pinned.
- Album and Music are now one Media category, with a built-in screenshot viewer
  (A for fullscreen, Y hands off to the system album).
- The ribbon background was rewritten: it is a real surface now, with layers at
  different depths and colours, its own motion per layer, up to 12 layers, and
  free vertical placement.

 Everywhere else

- Language- can be set by hand under Theming > Language instead of only
  following the console.
- Icon background opacity- slider in the theme editor.
- Minimal is the default icon pack, and it is complete: new gear, music,
  games, homebrew and media icons. The old "settings" icon was a wifi symbol.
- New sounds: confirm, click and back. Drop confirm.wav, click.wav and
  back.wav (or .mp3) into slaunch/sounds/. startup replaces opening.

 Fixes

- The menu is usable immediately.- Widget loading, the audio mixer and the
  sound files used to run on the main thread right after the first frame, which
  froze the menu for several seconds every time it appeared. That work now runs
  on a worker.
- Fully transparent colours were being drawn fully opaque, so an opacity of zero
  meant "solid" and every fade that reached zero flashed. Fixed.
- Untextured shapes were not drawn at all on this renderer, which is why parts
  of a box could look see-through.
- The album viewer scrolls smoothly instead of jumping.
- Backing out of a screen opened from Flow's menu returns to that menu instead
  of dropping you on the shelf.
- Flow no longer runs the console out of memory. It was holding around 145 MB of
  decoded image data, which starved other screens of the memory they needed and
  left them rendering black - opening a theme to edit it was the easiest way to
  see it. It now holds about 19 MB.

 Notes

- The images on the back of a box are SteamGridDB "heroes" - wide key art, not
  screenshots. SteamGridDB does not host screenshots, so real ones need a
  different source.
- Cover matching is by name, so an occasional wrong edition is expected. Replace
  the file in slaunch/covers/ to fix one by hand.

v0.8.0
The cross-media bar comes to sLaunch. New XMB mode (Theming > UI mode) does the PSP thing properly: categories ride a bar across the screen, your games hang below the selected one, and the whole thing is touch-driven - tap a category to open it, drag the column to flick through, tap an entry twice to launch.

Two long-standing annoyances are gone. Closing a homebrew now brings you back to the menu instead of relaunching the homebrew forever, and Restart / Power off now actually restart and power off instead of leaving the console in a weird half-asleep state.

Icon packs are in: drop PNG sets into slaunch/icon_packs// and switch between them in Theming > Icon pack. A clean Minimal pack by @meepcat55 ships in the box. Themes also gained an icon background colour, so packs sit right on any look.

sLaunch now speaks Russian, Japanese, German, Spanish and Chinese - it follows your console's language automatically, and slaunch/lang/template.txt is there if you want to add yours. Korean and Chinese consoles get their proper system font too, and a full Noto Sans CJK is bundled under Theming > Fonts.

Also: dragging anywhere now moves the content under your finger (not the cursor), taps in submenus land where you actually tap, and the welcome screen slimmed down to a quiet two lines that fade in and out.

Install:- run sInstaller.nro, or extract slaunch-v0.8.0-sd.zip to your SD root. Reboot after.

v0.7.0
sLaunch now says hello. On boot (and right after setup) you get a welcome screen that greets you by your Switch profile name over the opening jingle, with a different line each time. Don't want it? Theming > Welcome screen.

You can also clean up the menu now - every system entry (Album, Browser, Settings, Power, Homebrew...) can be shown or hidden in Theming > Menu entries. Theming itself stays put so you can always get back.

New Random game entry: it rolls through your library like a slot machine, lands on something, and launches it.

Setup got restyled to match the rest of the menu instead of looking like its own thing.
